newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka rupee ranged due to high supply of dollars.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka rupee ranged due to high supply of dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee moved little against the dollar in early Tuesday trade, as the market was well supplied with dollars, dealers said.
At 0430 GMT the rupee was at 58.49 to the dollar, after opening at 58.48. The rupee closed at 58.47 on Monday.
"Only an above average import bill will make a difference to the exchange rate, because the market is still well supplied with dollars," said an American Expres Bank dealer.
Dealers say net foreign inflows through the Colombo Stock Exchange over the last four to five weeks, have been mainly responsible for the market being well offered with dollars.
The Central Bank, meanwhile pushed up the dollar by two local cents in line with overseas gains, they said. Buying and selling prices were at 58.4768 and 59.6582.
"Call money rates being low and the Central Bank further easing the overnight repor rate today, has also cut the cost of holding dollars," said a Hongkong Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed down the repo rate to 8.75 percent from nine percent, on Tuesday.
Overnight call money rates were at 9.5 percent, after opening at 10, dealers said.
